route.name: Two-stage (PCSA)
route.whatItIs: A contractor is appointed early under a pre-construction services agreement on fees and prelims, helps develop the design, then prices the works open-book for the second stage.
route.bestWhen: Complex, occupied or phased work, or poor existing information, where early contractor input to sequencing and buildability pays off.
route.watchOuts: Less price competition at the second stage. Needs a strong cost consultant to test the price. Scope creep if not controlled.

model.name: Lump sum
model.whatItIs: One agreed price for a defined scope; the contractor carries the risk of its own pricing.
model.bestWhen: Scope and design are well defined and the client wants a firm price at award.
model.watchOuts: Unclear or changing scope leads to variations and claims. Contractors add risk allowances where information is poor.

contract.jct: JCT Pre-Construction Services Agreement (PCSA), then JCT DB (or SBC)
contract.nec4: First stage under NEC4 Professional Service Contract (PSC); construction under ECC Option A
contract.notes: Test the second-stage price against benchmarks before signing.

routeToMarket.name: Selective tender
routeToMarket.whatItIs: A shortlist of 4–6 suitable contractors is invited to tender.
routeToMarket.bestWhen: The client wants competition among contractors of proven capability.
routeToMarket.watchOuts: Public bodies above the threshold need a compliant procedure (e.g. competitive flexible) to shortlist. Prequalification takes time.

route.name: Traditional
route.whatItIs: The client's design team completes the design; contractors then price and build it. The client keeps design control.
route.bestWhen: Design can be completed before tender; cost certainty and design quality matter more than speed.
route.watchOuts: Slowest route to site. Gaps in the design become client variations. Little contractor input to buildability.

model.name: Remeasurement
model.whatItIs: Priced against approximate quantities or a schedule of rates; the work is measured as built and paid at the tendered rates.
model.bestWhen: The type of work is known but not its quantity — repairs, refurbishment with hidden conditions, or rolling programmes.
model.watchOuts: Final cost is only known at the end. Needs a reliable estimate of quantities and regular measurement.

contract.nec4: ECC Option B (priced contract with bill of quantities); Term Service Contract (TSC) for a programme
contract.notes: Regular measurement needed through the works.

routeToMarket.name: Framework — mini-competition
routeToMarket.whatItIs: A competition among contractors already appointed to a public-sector framework.
routeToMarket.bestWhen: Public clients who want competition with pre-vetted contractors and standard terms, faster than an open tender.
routeToMarket.watchOuts: Public and eligible bodies only. Check the lot's scope, value band, region and expiry. Framework fees may apply.

aiProse.executiveSummary: This feasibility study examines the refurbishment of Hargreaves Teaching Block, a three-storey 1960s education building at Example University in Birmingham, covering 1200 m² GIFA. The project will replace life-expired mechanical, electrical and plumbing services, upgrade fire safety, improve thermal performance to support net-zero objectives, and create modern flexible teaching space. The estimated total project cost is £1,613,000 to £1,973,000 excluding VAT, with Grade A confidence. The target date of 1 September 2028 is at risk; asbestos and ageing services present material delivery challenges.
keyFindings: The works cost mid-point is £1,138,000 with a range of £1,024,000 to £1,252,000; construction duration is 30 weeks within a 92-week total programme including design and procurement.
The target date of 1 September 2028 is not achievable; the 92-week programme completes approximately 6 weeks later, around 16 October 2028.
The stated budget of £4,500,000 including fees and VAT is sufficient, with approximately £2,132,000 headroom above the estimated range.
Asbestos is known or suspected in the building; a refurbishment and demolition survey is essential before Stage 2 design to confirm scope and cost.
The preferred option for the client to consider is a two-stage procurement route with lump-sum commercial model, which suits complex occupied phased work and minimises disruption.
scopeAssumptions: External plant space for the air source heat pump system is included within the heating and hot water scope.
The building was last refurbished in 2011 when the roof was recovered; windows on the south elevation were replaced in 2016, but north elevation windows and all services remain original.
Works are confined to university vacation and holiday windows only, excluding examination periods in January and May–June.
aiProse.costNarrative: The works cost reflects full replacement of mechanical, electrical, plumbing and fire safety systems across 1200 m² GIFA, together with strip-out, asbestos removal, and complete internal and external finishes. Preliminaries are elevated by partial occupation, restricted working hours and a phased programme. Professional fees account for the M&E-heavy scope and BREEAM compliance requirements.
aiProse.roiNarrative: The project cost mid-point of £1,794,000 against annual energy and operational savings of £95,000 yields a simple payback of 18.9 years. The key financial risk is that actual savings may fall short of projections if occupancy patterns, energy prices or operational practice diverge from assumptions used in the benefit calculation.

constraints.title: Vacation-only working
constraints.text: Works confined to university vacation windows; examination blackouts in January and May–June will fragment the construction programme and extend duration.

constraints.title: Restricted working hours
constraints.text: Limited permitted hours on a single service road in the middle of campus will increase labour costs and may attract out-of-hours premiums.

constraints.title: Asbestos and services
constraints.text: Asbestos is known or suspected; ageing M&E systems of uncertain capacity and condition may require scope changes and cost increases during design.

constraints.title: Conservation area
constraints.text: The site lies in a conservation area; external alterations will likely require full planning consent with enhanced materials and detailing.

constraints.title: Target date at risk
constraints.text: The 92-week programme completes 6 weeks after the target date; acceleration will require additional cost or scope trade-offs.

nextSteps: Commission a refurbishment and demolition asbestos survey immediately to confirm scope, cost and programme impact before Stage 2 design begins.
Obtain pre-application advice from the conservation officer on external alterations, materials and detailing to avoid planning delays.
Confirm electrical supply capacity and DNO requirements for the air source heat pump system with the utility and building services engineer.
Agree detailed blackout dates and permitted working hours with the university; model programme phasing to fit vacation windows and confirm float requirements.
Evaluate the two-stage procurement route with the client and cost consultant; prepare a shortlist of contractors with experience in occupied educational refurbishment.

riskRegister.description: Works confined to vacation windows; programme spans multiple academic terms; risk of overrun into term time.
riskRegister.mitigation: Phase works to vacation windows; agree blackout dates with faculty; build programme float; consider out-of-hours working.

riskRegister.description: Restricted working hours extend construction duration and may attract premium or out-of-hours rates.
riskRegister.mitigation: Confirm permitted hours with the client; price out-of-hours working where programme-critical; reflect in Prelims.

riskRegister.description: Ageing or inadequate mechanical and electrical services: capacity, condition and compliance of existing plant and distribution are uncertain and may need more replacement than assumed.
riskRegister.mitigation: Commission an M&E condition and capacity survey at Stage 2; confirm supply capacity with the utility early.

riskRegister.description: Asbestos is known or suspected: licensed removal, notification periods and air testing add cost and time, and finds during strip-out can stop work.
riskRegister.mitigation: Commission a refurbishment and demolition asbestos survey before Stage 2 design; carry a provisional sum for removal until it reports.

riskRegister.description: Site is in a conservation area or under an Article 4 direction: external alterations are likely to need full planning, with enhanced materials and detailing.
riskRegister.mitigation: Seek pre-application advice from the conservation officer; assume full planning for external works; allow for enhanced materials when costing.

riskRegister.description: Heating and hot water: electrical capacity and DNO check raised by the selected scope.
riskRegister.mitigation: Investigate and confirm during Stage 2 design, and carry the outcome into the cost plan.

riskRegister.description: The 92-week programme includes 7 weeks float; target date of 1 September 2028 is at risk of overrun by approximately 6 weeks.
riskRegister.mitigation: Review acceleration options at Stage 2, including long-lead procurement of major plant and reuse of existing surveys where scope-relevant.

riskRegister.description: Multiple-phase delivery with 15% uplift for sequential handovers and re-mobilisation; phase split to be confirmed at Stage 2.
riskRegister.mitigation: Develop detailed phase plan and sequencing strategy at Stage 2; confirm with occupants and facilities team early.

aiProse.procurementNarrative: A two-stage procurement with a lump-sum commercial model and selective tender route suits this complex, occupied, phased refurbishment where early contractor input to sequencing and buildability will reduce disruption and cost risk. The alternative traditional route with remeasurement would suit if design can be completed before tender and final cost certainty is less critical than design quality and control.
procurementConsiderations: Two-stage procurement typically offers less price competition at the second stage, so a strong cost consultant must test the final price against benchmarks before signing.
Lump-sum contracts place pricing risk on the contractor; if scope or design changes, variations and claims can follow, so scope control is essential.
Selective tender requires prequalification of 4–6 contractors, which takes time; public bodies above the threshold must follow a compliant procedure to shortlist.
procurementConflicts: Two-stage procurement can provide less price certainty at the point of entering the second stage, as the final contract price is typically developed and agreed later in the process.
